messages.content: Determine the winner in a Poker game with John having a Hand of 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥ and Mike having 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠.

function.name: card_games_poker_determine_winner
function.description: Determines the winner in a game of Poker based on the cards in each players' hands. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hand1.description: The list of cards (as strings) in first player's hand. E.g ['10♠', 'J♠']

hand2.description: The list of cards (as strings) in second player's hand. E.g ['9♥', '10♥']

message.reasoning:
We need to determine poker winner between two hands.

John's hand: 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥. That's hearts flush? Actually it's all hearts but missing 9♥; so not straight flush because sequence would require 9♥ as well. It's a flush (hearts). Highest card King. So John's best five-card combination is a flush: high card K.

Mike's hand: 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠. All spades except no Ace or 8. This also forms a flush: spade flush. But does it form a straight? Let's check ranks: 9,10,J,Q,K -> that's a royal straight? Wait Royal Straight requires A-K-Q-J-T. Here we have 9-10-J-Q-K which is a straight from 9 to K inclusive. Yes this is a straight (5 consecutive values). In standard poker ranking, a straight beats a flush. However note that both are flushes too. But since they share same suits? They don't matter. We compare highest rank among categories:

Category: Straight vs Flush. Straight outranks flush. Therefore Mike wins.

But let's double-check if there might be better category like straight flush? For Mike: he has 9♠,10♠,J♠,Q♠,K♠ - yes those are all spades and consecutive. That makes a straight flush! Indeed a straight flush outrank anything else. John's hand is just a flush. So Mike definitely wins.

Thus answer: Mike wins.

Let's produce output accordingly.
